_comment: Calibration baseline for the stress gate. Each cell names its gate kind in `gate`: errorRate (the default when absent), okPerSec, or none (report-only). See README 'Thresholds'.
calibrationNote: MIXED PROVENANCE, on purpose, and the four cliff cells are now POST-674a59e1. The write-queue-cliff cells (create@100, delete@100, mixed@100, auth-signup@100) are RUNNER-calibrated from three stress-nightly.yml workflow_dispatch runs on a GitHub hosted ubuntu-latest runner, all three at 32157ef1: 33546159251, 33546896150, 33547744930. This SUPERSEDES the five-run calibration of 2026-08-31 (33452619048, 33464423811, 33466235356, 33466730516, 33467169270), which measured code from before 674a59e1 'shed write backpressure without formatting a stack trace'. That commit changed what every write cell measures, so the old numbers describe a server that no longer exists: latency improved sharply (create@100 p99 ~2500 -> 1489-1724ms, delete@100 p99 ~28 -> 12-26ms), the partially-saturated cells' error rates FELL a lot (mixed@100 worst 16.3934 -> 12.4837, auth-signup@100 worst 15.5589 -> 3.5994), and the two fully-saturated cells' rose slightly (create@100 97.7843 -> 98.3259, delete@100 99.0558 -> 99.5712) because cheaper rejection lets the closed-loop generator land more attempts inside the same 5s window. The ARMED gate went red on exactly that and nothing else: run 33546159251 failed delete@100 at 99.5712% against the old 99.5558% ceiling, by 0.0154pp, with no regression behind it. THREE observations is a THINNER basis than the five it replaces -- it is what exists at this sha, and it is stated rather than smoothed over. The other 26 cells keep their 2026-08-18 laptop calibration UNCHANGED: they read exactly 0.00% in all three post-fix runs, as well as in all five pre-fix runner runs and all three laptop runs, so there is again nothing to recalibrate. p99ObservedMs for these four is refreshed from the same three runs -- it had still held the 2026-08-18 laptop numbers, which is misleading trend data for cells whose latency moved this much; p99 remains NOT gated. TOLERANCES. Three cells take this file's rule -- worst observation plus one full measured spread, rounded up to the next whole percentage point: create@100 +1.0pp (spread 0.2196), mixed@100 +6.0pp (spread 5.5825), auth-signup@100 +4.0pp (spread 3.5994). mixed@100 and auth-signup@100 were +8.0pp and +16.0pp against the old, much wider pre-fix spreads; a 31.56% ceiling on a cell that now reads 0.00-3.60% asserts nothing, so both are narrowed to their new spreads. create@100 needs an override at all only because its new baseline of 98.3259 plus the 2.0pp default is 100.33, which check_thresholds.dart refuses as a dead gate. delete@100 cannot take the rule: at a 99.5712 baseline only 0.4288pp is physically left below 100 and one whole point does not fit, so its headroom is bounded by what remains -- toleranceOverridePP 0.25 for a ceiling of 99.8212%, which is 1.41 measured spreads above its worst observation (where the old 0.5pp was only 0.45 of the spread it faced, which is why it flapped) and 0.1788pp under the maximum. That 0.18pp is the entire live range this cell has. See README 'Thresholds' -- error rate is close to blind for create@100 and delete@100 and that is a design question, not a calibration one. UPDATE 2026-09-01, LATER THE SAME DAY: that design question is answered. create@100 now carries gate "okPerSec" and delete@100 gate "none"; each cell's own calibrationNote has the runs, the shas and the arithmetic. Their errorRate fields above are kept as trend data and no longer gate anything. mixed@100 and auth-signup@100 are unchanged: they are partially saturated and error rate still moves there.

policy.gatedMetric: per cell (`gate`): errorRate by default, okPerSec for create@100, none for delete@100
policy.p99Rationale: NOT gated. Across the same three runs the p99 spread was 139% at the median and 2178% at the worst cell. A p99 gate at any threshold those runs support would flap, and a flapping gate gets muted. p99 is REPORTED for trend only.

create@100.calibrationNote: GATED ON SUCCESSFUL THROUGHPUT, not error rate. At ~98.3% errors by design (a 64-deep write queue against a 100-user zero-backoff closed loop, with a reject costing 0.14ms against 0.33ms to serve) the error-rate ceiling had 1.0pp of live range before the 100% wall and moved the WRONG way when the server improved. ok/s = (total - errors) / wallTimeMs * 1000 from five post-674a59e1 stress-nightly.yml workflow_dispatch runs on hosted ubuntu-latest: 33546159251 at 32157ef1 (260 ok / 5057ms = 51.4139), 33546896150 at 32157ef1 (179 / 5064 = 35.3476), 33547744930 at 32157ef1 (218 / 5059 = 43.0915), 33549701544 at 0404e063 (221 / 5059 = 43.6845), 33552772241 at 0404e063 (195 / 5063 = 38.5147). Worst 35.3476, best 51.4139, spread 16.0663. Floor = worst - one full spread = 35.3476 - 16.0663 = 19.2813, rounded DOWN to 19 (the rule: never below 1). A run that lands under 19 successful creates per second is a real collapse, not calibration noise: it is more than one whole measured spread below the worst of five. The errorRatePercentBaseline / errorRateObserved / toleranceOverridePP fields on this cell are trend data from the three-run error-rate calibration and are NOT consulted by the gate. Still knownBad: rejecting ~98% of writes at concurrency 100 is not thereby acceptable.

delete@100.calibrationNote: REPORT-ONLY, on purpose, because neither metric this file can gate measures anything here. Error rate sits at ~99.5% by design with 0.18pp of live range before the 100% wall, and successful throughput is not a throughput: delete@100 completes EXACTLY 64 requests in every run regardless of duration (64 in all five runner runs; locally 64 at both 5s and 15s, see .showrunner/scratch/write-queue-write-queue/FINDINGS.md). Steady-state successful deletes at concurrency 100 are zero; the 64 is the end-of-run drain of a write queue pinned at _maxQueuedWrites, landed when the generator stops starting iterations and the 64 in-flight users finish their create-then-delete against an emptying queue. So its ok/s is the queue depth divided by wall time (~12.5/s at 5s, ~4.3/s at 15s no matter what the server does) and any floor on it would gate the constant 64, not the server. Both numbers are still printed for trend. The errorRate fields on this cell are the three-run calibration kept as trend data; they gate nothing. Still knownBad. The way to make this cell assert something is to change what it measures (a delete scenario that does not need two consecutive admissions per iteration), not to pick a threshold.
